title: If this single database crashes, your Kubernetes cluster dies
caption: etcd holds the state of your entire Kubernetes cluster. Have you ever restored an etcd snapshot?

scenes.vo: Your entire Kubernetes cluster relies on one single brain that remembers everything. Meet etcd, the key value database holding cluster state.
scenes.heading: ETCD

scenes.vo: Think of etcd like a safe company vault storing every single truth. If it dies, the whole management team loses memory.
scenes.heading: THE BRAIN
scenes.line: Like a company vault storing all truth

scenes.vo: When you apply a file, only the API server writes that change to etcd. Nothing else touches it directly.
scenes.heading: HOW IT SAVES STATE
scenes.note: ONLY API SERVER TALKS TO ETCD

scenes.vo: Never back up etcd by hand. Use etcdctl to save a consistent snapshot file that can restore your saved cluster.
scenes.heading: THE TRICK

scenes.vo: So etcd is the key value store, your single source of truth. Always take snapshots! Follow for more Kubernetes tips.
scenes.heading: ETCD
